pairing_rules.reason: Solids provide a clean anchor that lets stripes stand out naturally.
A solid piece grounds the visual geometry of checks without competing.
Solid colours balance prominent floral prints and prevent visual clutter.
Solid garments anchor playful polka dots for a well-proportioned outfit.
Rich paisley designs require a calm solid companion to avoid overwhelming the eye.
Sharp geometric patterns pop cleanly against neutral or solid backdrops.
Abstract prints make an effective artistic focal point alongside solid garments.
Two solids create timeless color-blocked or monochromatic looks.
Competing directional grids create high visual vibration that clashes.
Can work when subtle pinstripes sit beneath organic florals sharing a common hue.
Rigid lines and round repeating dots produce jarring pattern interference.
Dense swirling motifs conflict aggressively with linear stripe rhythms.
Linear elements can harmonize if stripe widths distinctly contrast geometric shapes.
Strict linear stripes feel disjointed against erratic abstract forms.
Heavy grid structures fight organic blooming botanicals for visual dominance.
Squares against circles create dizzying geometric dissonance.
Both motifs carry heavy visual density and quickly overwhelm an ensemble.
Acceptable only when check size is significantly larger than micro-geometric accents.
Both prints are intricate and busy, creating excessive decorative conflict.
Organic curves can offset structured geometric lines if one is understated.
Multiple hard repeating shapes cause confusing focal tension.

scale_rule: When mixing two prints, use different scales (one large, one small) and share at least one common colour.
